architecture_decisions.title: Assessment service is backend-only — mobile does not call it directly
architecture_decisions.context: Assessment involves CITC, geolocation, SIMAH, and decision engine — all server-side operations triggered after application submission.
architecture_decisions.decision: Mobile calls POST /applications/{id}/submit on applications-service. Applications-service orchestrates assessment-service internally via REST. Mobile polls GET /applications/{id} for status updates.
architecture_decisions.consequences: Simpler mobile architecture (2 new API clients not 3). Assessment logic fully server-side. Mobile needs polling or push notification for status updates.

architecture_decisions.title: PCI-DSS SAQ A via payment processor hosted fields
architecture_decisions.context: Card data (PAN, expiry, CVV) must never touch BridgeNow's backend or mobile app storage per PCI-DSS.
architecture_decisions.decision: Use payment processor's JavaScript SDK (hosted iframe) for card capture. Only the tokenised reference is stored in DebitCards table.
architecture_decisions.consequences: BridgeNow remains SAQ A (lowest PCI scope). Card collection screen uses WebView/iframe. Token stored encrypted at rest.

architecture_decisions.title: Offer calculation is server-side only
architecture_decisions.context: Offer amount depends on verified income, SIMAH DBR, product parameters, and business rules that must not be exposed to the client.
architecture_decisions.decision: Mobile displays read-only offer data from GET /applications/{id}/offer. All calculation happens in offers-service using assessment results + product config.
architecture_decisions.consequences: No business logic leakage to mobile. Offer tampering impossible. Mobile is a pure display layer for financial data.

architecture_decisions.title: Cooling-off period tracked server-side with UTC timestamps
architecture_decisions.context: 24-hour SAMA cooling-off must be accurate regardless of client clock manipulation.
architecture_decisions.decision: Contract.CoolingPeriodEndsAt is set server-side as UTC. Mobile displays countdown by comparing server timestamp (from GET /applications/{id}) against device clock. Timer is informational only — actual expiry enforced server-side.
architecture_decisions.consequences: Tamper-proof cooling-off. Mobile timer may drift slightly from server but disbursement pipeline only proceeds after server-side expiry check.
architecture_decisions.kb_reference: PD5 (right to withdraw), SAMA cooling-off regulation

architecture_decisions.title: Separate database per service for Sprint 2
architecture_decisions.context: Three new services need data stores. EA2 mandates database-per-service.
architecture_decisions.decision: applications-db (LoanApplications), assessment-db (AssessmentResults), offers-db (Offers, Contracts, DebitCards, Disbursements). InMemory for dev, SQL Server for staging/prod.
architecture_decisions.consequences: No cross-service joins. Services communicate via REST APIs. Data consistency via eventual consistency patterns.
architecture_decisions.kb_reference: EA2 (microservices), EA4 (data management), MS3 (database per service)

risks.mitigation: Circuit breaker (3 failures → open 120s), retry with exponential backoff, application held in 'Pending' state, mock SIMAH for dev/test

risks.mitigation: Spike in Sprint 2 week 1 to validate SDK in Android WebView. Fallback: native card form with immediate tokenisation API call (higher PCI scope)

risks.risk: Open Banking redirect flow UX — user leaves app and may not return
risks.mitigation: Deep link callback to resume application. Auto-save before redirect. 30-minute session timeout with resume capability

reasoning: Sprint 2 is a major expansion: 3 new microservices, 9 new screens, 7 external integrations. The Sprint 1 foundation provides solid reusable patterns (Clean Architecture, MediatR CQRS, Compose MVVM, design system, DI modules) that significantly reduce boilerplate. The highest-risk items are the payment processor SDK integration (PCI-DSS hosted fields in Compose WebView) and SIMAH API reliability. The dependency order ensures the application form (EP-02) can be delivered independently, providing a deployable increment even if EP-03 assessment/disbursement encounters delays. All 23 stories map to at least one change_impact entry. No story is orphaned.
